name: Jawaharlal Nehru
summary: Nehru led India as a parliamentary democrat committed to a secular state, a planned mixed economy with a dominant public sector in heavy industry, and a non-aligned foreign policy. He called himself a socialist but rejected class war and dictatorship, favouring peaceful, democratic change. He drove Hindu personal law reform, linguistic states, and military action over Hyderabad and Goa while working for disarmament.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Told chief ministers that private enterprise was increasingly hedged in by state enterprise and that the nineteenth-century idea of private enterprise had faded; he wanted a plan that private enterprise must fit into, while keeping a role for it.

public-ownership.rationale: His five-year plans placed basic and heavy industry (steel, coal, power) in the public sector. He chose to concentrate state resources on vital new industries rather than nationalise many existing ones, so the position is supportive but selective.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Said big disparities should go and a socialist pattern needed; Congress under his leadership in 1953 called for taxation to reduce inequalities and welcomed the Estate Duty Bill.

property-fundamental.rationale: Drove zamindari abolition and said ownership must fit the national plan, treating property as subordinate to social ends.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Accepted private enterprise in many fields but said it must fit the national plan and carry the controls considered necessary.

state-harmful.rationale: Built and used the state as the main instrument of development and reform.

decide-locally.rationale: Stressed panchayati raj and village-level self-government among urgent tasks for chief ministers.

more-religion-public.rationale: Condemned religious bigotry and communalism in public life and rejected communal organisations' agitation over cow slaughter and the Hindu Code.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Discovery of India celebrates Indian cultural continuity, and he urged being true to the country while learning from the world.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Said the United Nations, despite weaknesses, should be supported and allowed to develop into some kind of world government or world order.

free-trade.rationale: Pursued import substitution and protectionist policies rather than open trade.

limit-growth.rationale: Aimed for about five per cent annual growth, arguing slow growth would not keep pace with population.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Wrote of science and modern technology as essential to meeting poverty and building a modern India.

revolution-justified.rationale: Asked whether classless society could come through violence or peaceful methods and chose democratic, peaceful change.

central-planning.rationale: Chaired the Planning Commission and ran India by five-year plans, crediting Soviet heavy-industry success while rejecting its costs and rigidity; he held a mixed economy with a dominant plan rather than a fully centrally planned one.

tax-inheritance.rationale: His government's 1953 Estate Duty Bill, welcomed in the Congress resolution he led, taxed estates at death as a means of reducing inequality.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Import-substitution policy with subsidies and protection for key industries.

state-directs-investment.rationale: His plans directed investment into steel, iron, coal and power, and he said the foundations of basic and heavy industries must be laid by the state because defence rests on them.

one-party-rule.rationale: Led a multiparty parliamentary system, said he had no intention of banning the Communist Party for its legitimate activities, and contrasted China's system with parliamentary democracy.

democracy-best.rationale: Chose parliamentary democracy for India; argued that nationalisation without political democracy only yields a different kind of exploitation.

right-to-secede.rationale: Used military force over Hyderabad (1948) and defended Kashmir's accession; opposed separatist movements, including Dravidistan demands.

political-violence-never.rationale: Non-violence was central to the Gandhian movement he followed, but he accepted armed force for defence and used it over Hyderabad, Kashmir and Goa.

separate-church-state.rationale: Described a secular State in which no religion is favoured and every religion has full freedom and equal honour; his secularism means equal respect rather than hostility.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Drove the Hindu Code Bills reforming Hindu personal law against orthodox opposition, in the name of modernisation and national unity.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred: he treated courts, defence and policing as state functions and wanted a strong army, navy and air force.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Held that India is a secular State for all communities and that everything that separates is bad, everything that joins is good.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Declared in 1955 he wanted a classless society and in 1928 that the economic programme must aim at removing all economic inequalities; he also stressed equal opportunity.

limit-population.rationale: Repeatedly named population growth a serious problem that absorbs production gains and called for it to be addressed.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Drove rapid industrialisation as the path out of poverty.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Said the plan should not rest on dogma but on existing facts, and urged thinking about the problem rather than getting lost in labels.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Rejected dictatorship and class war; held that economic change without political democracy yields another kind of exploitation.

collective-farming.rationale: Pressed for cooperative farming (with individual or joint ownership) and in 1950 supported collective farms on state waste land, but rejected Soviet-style compulsion; the evidence points both ways.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred: he built a progressive-tax, planned welfare state and called for taxation measures to cut inequality.

positive-liberty.rationale: Described the content of democracy as economic democracy too, and tied freedom to ending poverty and inequality of opportunity.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: India recognised Israel in 1950 only because it was a fact; he delayed it to avoid offending Arab states, which shows no endorsement of a right to a state.

national-self-determination.rationale: Led India's independence struggle and wrote on self-determination as a principle.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Urged science and scientific temper as essential for all; wrote that organised religion today is largely an empty form, though he valued the spiritual.

class-collaboration.rationale: Told chief ministers that India encouraged no class war and did not wish to injure any group or class, a lesson he took from Gandhi.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Condemned racial discrimination against Indians in the dominions and denounced South African apartheid in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Expanded state functions: planning, public-sector industry, land reform, social legislation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Moved the Objectives Resolution guaranteeing equality of status, opportunity and before the law; said every citizen of the secular state has equal liberty and opportunity.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Wikipedia reports he likely favoured a uniform code but accepted that personal laws were tied to religious identity, so he codified Hindu law first.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Objectives Resolution he moved said all power and authority of sovereign India are derived from the people.

priority-to-poor.rationale: In the Tryst with Destiny speech he said the service of India meant ending poverty, ignorance, disease and inequality of opportunity for the suffering millions.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: His government passed the Preventive Detention Act 1950 against hoarders and subversives, yet he said he was unhappy about detaining Sheikh Abdullah; the record is mixed.

minority-language-support.rationale: Reorganised states on linguistic lines and protected other languages through the Eighth Schedule and English's continued use.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: In the Objectives Resolution speech he said the Resolution concerned economic democracy as well as political democracy, and stood for socialism.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Moved the Objectives Resolution in the Constituent Assembly and worked within it to frame India's constitution.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Opposed nuclear weapons and tests and did not develop them for India.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Said private enterprise must fit the national plan and carry such controls as are needed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Used military force to annex Hyderabad in 1948 and fought Pakistan over Kashmir.

land-redistribution.rationale: His government abolished zamindari and jagirdari estates (with compensation) and advocated land ceilings; the ceilings largely failed.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Pressed abolition of jagirdari and zamindari estates and integrated princely states, though privy purses were kept.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rejected British rule as exploitative and racially discriminatory and campaigned for independence.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: In 1959 he wrote that capitalist structure has undergone and keeps undergoing change through democratic and other forces, while class struggles and inequality remain.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: His government enacted laws criminalising caste discrimination and insisted every citizen has equal liberty and opportunity.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Moved the Objectives Resolution promising guaranteed and secured justice, equality, and freedoms of thought, expression, belief and worship, which became the basis of the Constitution's fundamental rights.

single-official-language.rationale: Backed Hindi for all-India purposes but said it must not seem imposed at the expense of other languages, and enacted the Official Languages Act 1963 to keep English.

religious-nation.rationale: Rejected defining India by religion; said it was a free secular State where every religion has equal honour.

defeat-communism.rationale: Pursued peaceful co-existence and refused to join anti-communist blocs.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Led the Hindustani camp in the Constituent Assembly against a purely Sanskritised Hindi.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Refused to ban the Communist Party nationally, though his government used preventive detention and arrests against some opponents and communal groups.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Discovery of India criticises British economic exploitation and racial discrimination in empire; he led the independence movement.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Invoked Gandhi's view that taking the sword was better than surrender, and kept and modernised the army, navy and air force.

rich-first.rationale: His stated ideal was equal opportunities and removing big disparities rather than letting some prosper first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Architect of non-alignment: said India keeps away from power blocs and military alliances.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Discovery of India traces India's culture in continuous development from the Indus Valley to the present.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Averse to war and called Goa aggression by the Portuguese, but used force over Hyderabad, Kashmir and Goa; mixed.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: he said India would tolerate no communalism and was building a secular State with equal citizenship, which excludes separate religious electorates.

arms-reduction.rationale: Campaigned for disarmament and a ban on nuclear tests, calling nuclear weapons frightful engines of destruction.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Campaigned for and secured the Hindu Succession Act 1956 and related Hindu Code laws that expanded women's inheritance and legal rights.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: In 1947-48 pledged a plebiscite in Kashmir with protections and said he would abide by it; by 1953 he declined one, and rejected a plebiscite on Himalayan territory in 1960.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Said India would not tolerate any communalism and was building a secular State where every religion had equal honour.

notes: Nehru's attitude to planning and nationalisation is the mature mixed-economy position of the 1950s. On Kashmir he pledged a plebiscite in 1947-48 but declined one from 1953; the latter is treated as his mature position. His autobiography on the death penalty is ambivalent.
